versioning: minor versions for scheduling-model, state/schema or external-side-effect changes; patch versions for compatible additions. 0.7.0: measured memory as a scheduling input (admission guard, memory pressure, --mem auto), schema 9, GitHub posts, event-driven low-priority worker.
node_config: config/zenobia-node.json: the live 0.6.3 node.json (one pool 0-7 + GPU, aliases, default_mem 4G) plus memory, github, launch.idle_seconds 30 and partitions[0].min_mem 256M; config/zenobia-16core-node.json the same on 0-15 (its default_mem lowered to 4G as on the 8-core node)

database_schema.change: columns added to jobs: mem_current_bytes, mem_peak_bytes, mem_peak_source, mem_sampled_at, mem_series_json, cpu_usage_usec, mem_auto_json, github_json, github_phase, github_attempts, github_next_unix, github_error, github_done, github_posted_at, github_comment_id; index jobs_github_pending_idx; no existing column changes. Rollback sets user_version back to 8 in place. The migration also redacts secret-pattern values in stored job environments (queue_meta env_scrubbed_through); install redacts finished jobs' spec.json and its backup copy.

systemd_unit: simqueue.service: Nice=10, CPUWeight=20, IOSchedulingClass=idle, MemoryHigh=96M, MemoryMax=128M (0.6.3: Nice=5)
features: security: the job environment is an allowlist (HOME, USER, LOGNAME, LANG, PATH, TZ, SIMQUEUE_*, --export NAMES|ALL, -e); names matching *TOKEN*, *SECRET*, *PASSWORD*, *KEY*, GITHUB_*, ACTIONS_*, RUNNER_* are never taken from the environment; given with -e they reach the job but are stored <redacted> (value in a mode-600 secrets file until the job ends; spec.json redacted then); the schema-9 migration scrubs older rows

event-driven worker: select() on <state>/worker.wake (clients after submit/cancel/..., the job wrapper's stop-post hook), data_version of its own persistent SQLite connection for other writers; passes every poll_seconds only while something must be watched, else at most every launch.idle_seconds (30 s); between passes only file reads (job cgroups, /proc/meminfo); systemd queried only for units that need it, all units every 5 minutes

memory tracking: memory.current/memory.peak of every running job unit every memory.sample_seconds (3 s), bounded min/max-per-minute series, peak and CPU time recorded by the unit at its end (jobwrap status/stop-post usage), shown in simq show (now, peak, CPU time, history), simq list (MEM column) and simq partitions (node available memory, water marks, per-job request against actual, outside-queue use)

--mem auto: 1.25 x the largest of the last 5 peaks of jobs with the same name (else name family, same core count preferred), OOM kills counted at their limit, rounded up to 256M, within min_mem..max_mem; default without history; idempotent replays keep their job
over-request warning on submit (>= 2x and >= 2G above the recent peak)
admission guard: a start needs request <= MemAvailable - margin (default: the high-water mark) - unallocated requests of jobs started < 60 s ago; reservations stay primary

memory pressure: MemAvailable below max(2G, 7%) stops dispatch, preempts borrow jobs by --on-preempt (frozen ones requeued after 120 s), records the job that grew against its request; owner jobs never stopped; resumes at max(4G, 12%)

GitHub reporting: --github-status OWNER/REPO@SHA:CONTEXT (repeatable), --github-comment OWNER/REPO#PR, --github-summary PATH (SIMQ_SUMMARY) on submit and run; statuses per transition (pending/success/failure/error with runtime, peak memory, exit code or reason, <= 140 chars); one PR comment edited in place (<!-- simq-job:N -->); job text sanitized against mentions and issue references; one posting thread in the worker with backoff retries; token from token_file or gh auth token, memory only
run-tests.py --in-job (inside a queue job) and --pure; tools/bench-overhead.py

overhead.method: each worker in its own transient user unit with the properties it is installed with; cgroup cpu.stat usage over 10 minutes after a 30 s warm-up; all four at once; busy = 2-core pool, 2 running and 10 queued sleep jobs
